page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.medium is a compute-optimized instance powered by a dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor. This server features 1 physical core and 1 vCPU running at 2.6 GHz on the ARMv8 architecture, supported by 2.0 GB of system memory. The hardware configuration includes a bundled 59 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1515.58 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1430.0. However, due to its single-core design, multi-core benchmarks scale identically, resulting in poor multi-core ratings. Memory bandwidth is limited, with read-only large block transfers reaching 30.49 GB/sec and write operations at 10.89 GB/sec. Single-threaded tasks like bzip3 decompression perform at an average rate of 9.19 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput is measured at 1.88 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c7gd.medium offers a low-cost entry point to ARM64-based compute resources with high-speed local NVMe storage. The primary tradeoff is the single-threaded limitation, which restricts its utility for parallelized workloads or heavy multi-core processing.

This instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic web serving, development environments, and applications that benefit from low-latency local NVMe storage without requiring high memory capacity.
